subject: Customer DPA: Medisync redlines + counsel questions (round 1)
messages:
From: Amanda Liu <amanda@medisync.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: contract.ops@medisync.com
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Initial redline: Medisync DPA (round 1)

Hi Jordan / Laura,

Thanks for the call this morning. Attaching our legal team’s first-pass redline of the DPA — we’ve flagged the sections that are non-negotiable for Medisync (audit windows, subprocessor carveouts, and the EU->US transfer language). A couple of quick notes up front: 

- We mark Section 5 (Subprocessors) as a hard requirement for prior written consent for any subprocessors accessing patient data.
- We’ve proposed a customer-favoring retention schedule in Annex B.
- For transfers, the redline references SCCs but asks Redwood to accept a separate EU-US Addendum.

Files: [Attachment: Medisync_DPA_Round1_redline.pdf (PDF, 74 KB)]

Do you have a preferred execution flow? Our contract.ops team prefers AdobeSign, and they’ve included a link in the email below.

Amanda Liu
Head of Legal Operations, Medisync Health
amanda@medisync.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Liu <amanda@medisync.com>, PrivacyCounsel LLP <privacy@pcounsel.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redline: Medisync DPA (round 1)

Amanda — thanks for sending. Laura and I reviewed the redline and routed to privacy counsel for a technical read; looping in PrivacyCounsel LLP for visibility and suggested edits. High-level reactions from Redwood: 

- Prior consent for all subprocessors will be a blocker for us operationally. We can commit to notice + opt-out carveouts for changes that materially affect security or data residency, plus a short approval window for critical subprocessors.
- Retention: we’re open to clarifying the retention timeline for PHI, but we need alignment on what constitutes a record "in-scope" vs. telemetry/metrics.
- Transfers: we can accept SCCs but prefer to implement the EU-US transfer via SCCs with a narrow, documented Addendum rather than a full BCR or unilateral addendum. Counsel: please propose redline text for a transfer clause that covers: SCC attachment, risk-based supplementary measures, and an administrative contact for DSRs.

Execution: Redwood is flexible on e-sign. If Medisync prefers AdobeSign, that works — we’ll just need a final consolidated PDF with signature blocks and the SCC exhibit appended. Marissa, can you prepare a consolidated counterproposal (track-changes) and an AdobeSign-ready package? Target: internal review complete by Wednesday EOD.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior GTM Counsel, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]
[Attachment: internal_notes_subproc_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 24 KB)]

From: PrivacyCounsel LLP <privacy@pcounsel.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Amanda Liu <amanda@medisync.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redline: Medisync DPA (round 1) — counsel comments

Jordan / Amanda — attached is an annotated version of Medisync’s redline with proposed compromise language. Key recommendations: 

1) Subprocessors — propose two-tier approach: (i) consent for subprocessors processing PHI or PII tied to EU data subjects; (ii) notice-within-30-days for lower-risk infrastructure providers. We give specific language to slot into Section 5.

2) Transfers — we recommend Redwood commit to SCCs (EU standard contractual clauses) appended as Annex C and add a short paragraph about supplementary measures (encryption in transit, limited personnel access, documented DPIAs where applicable). We add a customer-facing administrative contact for DSR escalation.

3) Audit clause — propose a defined, reasonable audit scope (annually, remote-first, 10 business days’ notice, redaction of unrelated data). 

4) Retention — recommend harmonized phrasing: Redwood will retain customer data per Exhibit B and purge within X days of termination unless retention is required by law — suggested X=90 (negotiable).

We’re not asking for a full BCR regime; SCCs + measured supplementary protections should be sufficient. Attached: [Attachment: SCCs_annotated-guide.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)]

If Medisync is comfortable, we can prepare a consolidated counter-DPA with tracked edits and a short negotiation memo explaining each compromise.

— Priya K., PrivacyCounsel LLP
privacy@pcounsel.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redline: Medisync DPA (round 1) — internal plan

Team — quick internal plan based on counsel’s notes: 

- Marissa: please assemble a consolidated DPA that: (a) accepts SCCs as Annex C, (b) includes the two-tier subprocessor language from counsel, (c) sets retention to 90 days for customer data post-termination with carveouts for law enforcement/regulated holds.
- I will draft a short negotiation memo listing must-haves vs. concessions (we should concede audit with restrictions; push back on prior consent requirement).
- Jordan: if you can confirm the administrative DSR contact and the supplementary measures language we’ll propose, I’ll package the AdobeSign envelope. Medisync prefers AdobeSign per their ops note — we’ll include both Redwood signature block and an Exhibit C with SCCs appended as PDF.

Timeline: consolidated DPA + memo by EOD Thursday (26 Jul). Marissa — please include a one-page summary for CS/ops in the package.

Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Liu <amanda@medisync.com>, contract.ops@medisync.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Jul 2028 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redline: Medisync DPA (round 1) — next steps and AdobeSign package

Amanda — thanks for your patience. Attached is Redwood’s consolidated counterproposal (track changes) and a one-page memo explaining the compromises. Highlights: 

- We accepted SCCs as Annex C and included an Annex reference for the EU transfer controls.
- Subprocessors: adopted counsel’s two-tier approach; customers will receive notice for new subprocessors and prior consent will be limited to subprocessors accessing PHI or EU-data-scoped content.
- Retention: 90 days for business data after termination, with lawful-hold carveouts.
- Audit: remote-first, limited scope, 10 business days’ notice, and the option for Redwood to produce redacted reports rather than full on-site access.

Please review the consolidated PDF and indicate whether Medisync wants to proceed with AdobeSign. If yes, use this link to start the signing flow: https://adobesign.example.com/request/ABC123. If Medisync prefers DocuSign or needs separate countersignature order, tell us and we can adapt.

Action items: 
- Medisync: confirm execution method + signatory name and email for the first signature.
- Redwood (Marissa): prepare final AdobeSign envelope with Exhibit C (SCCs) appended and include quick-capture summary for CS.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this week.

Jordan Blake
Senior GTM Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_DPA_counterproposal_round1.pdf (PDF, 85 KB)]
